skill.name: design-spec-extraction
skill.description: Extract structured design specifications from user-provided visual UI sources, including Figma exports, mockups, and screenshots. The skill guides a seven-pass workflow for layout, tokens, components, spacing, states, and accessibility notes.
skill.summary: Extract design tokens, layout, components, and accessibility notes from visual UI inputs.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, schema URLs, visual-design grid terminology, and user-provided screenshot references. Two directory-creation findings remain confirmed because the skill shows unquoted project-name placeholders in shell commands. A bundled audit_output.json also makes an untrusted safe-to-publish claim, and project names can influence output paths without explicit slug validation.

remediation.issue: Self-authored audit output claims the skill is safe to publish.
remediation.suggestion: Remove audit_output.json from the published skill or clearly mark it as non-authoritative sample output.

remediation.issue: Project names are inserted into output paths and shell examples without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a simple slug such as lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, and reject path separators or shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The bash mkdir examples use unquoted placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the AI tool filesystem API for directory creation, or quote and validate the project slug before any shell command.

remediation.issue: The skill handles screenshots and visual exports that may include sensitive information.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning to remove secrets, customer data, and private internal content before analysis.

content.user_title: Extract Design Specs from Visual Mockups
content.value_statement: Design handoff from screenshots and mockups can lose tokens, layout details, and accessibility notes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a seven-pass extraction into structured design specifications.
actual_capabilities: Extracts layout regions, grids, containers, and section bounds from visual UI inputs.
Identifies color palettes, semantic color roles, and visual style tokens.
Captures typography details such as font family, size, weight, and line height.
Builds a component hierarchy with bounding boxes, variants, and confidence notes.
Documents spacing, dimensions, interaction states, and accessibility observations.
Writes intermediate pass files and a final consolidated design specification.
limitations: Requires a user-provided image or export; it does not browse live sites by itself.
Measurements and colors are estimates when the source image has low resolution.
Hover, focus, and error states need separate images or clear user guidance.
Project names should be simple slugs to keep generated files in the intended folder.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Specs
use_cases.description: Convert a mockup into layout, token, and component notes before building a UI.

use_cases.title: Audit Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Check whether a visual design includes enough color, spacing, typography, and state detail for delivery.

use_cases.title: Document Existing Interfaces
use_cases.description: Turn approved product screens into structured references for tokens, components, and accessibility review.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-spec-extraction on the attached screen. Use project name product-home and produce the final design specification with a short summary.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Figma Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-spec-extraction on this Figma export. Focus on layout, color tokens, typography, and reusable components for developer handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Review Accessibility Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Run design-spec-extraction with extra attention to contrast, focus states, touch targets, labels, and semantic structure. Include uncertainty notes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple States
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-spec-extraction across these default, hover, error, and mobile screenshots. Consolidate shared tokens and document state differences.

output_examples.input: A desktop dashboard screenshot with navigation, cards, tables, and charts.
output: Layout regions identified for header, sidebar, main content, and chart area.
Color and typography tokens summarized with confidence levels.
Reusable card, table, button, and chart components documented.
Accessibility notes include contrast risks and missing visible labels.

output_examples.input: A mobile checkout mockup exported from a design tool.
output: Mobile viewport dimensions and stacked layout structure captured.
Spacing, radius, button, input, and error-state patterns described.
Implementation notes highlight uncertain measurements and required state screenshots.

output_examples.input: Several approved product screens for a design system review.
output: Shared tokens grouped by color, typography, spacing, and elevation.
Common components listed with variants and recommended naming.
Inconsistencies flagged for designer review before implementation.

best_practices: Use high-resolution images and crop out unrelated browser or desktop content when possible.
Use a simple project slug, such as checkout-flow, for generated output folders.
Validate the final specification against the provided schema before using it for implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not use screenshots that contain secrets, customer data, or private internal information.
Do not expect exact source design tokens from low-quality raster images.
Do not skip intermediate passes when the final specification needs traceable evidence.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: High-resolution Figma exports, UI mockups, and clear screenshots work best. Cropped images reduce unrelated noise.

faq.question: Does the skill browse live websites?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes visual inputs provided by the user and does not open websites on its own.

faq.question: Can it produce exact design tokens?
faq.answer: It estimates tokens from visible pixels and structure. Original design files are more accurate than screenshots.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It creates pass files and a final design specification under a project folder inside .design-specs.

faq.question: Is it suitable for accessibility review?
faq.answer: It can flag visible contrast, target size, label, and state issues, but it is not a full accessibility test.

faq.question: How should I protect sensitive designs?
faq.answer: Remove secrets, personal data, and private customer details before sharing screenshots with any AI tool.
